fidelity_limits: search.family_coordinate@1.0.0 supplies candidate ask/tell only: this stage produces no execution, no ranking and no acceptance decision.
A validated plan requires a future grant; current backend_solves budget is 0, so no batch runs and no candidate is promoted here.
Holding metrics are sampled over the final closed interval [0.30, 0.35] s (6 rows) with no continuous-time guarantee; missing samples would be unavailable, never a pass.
No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists; any candidate-versus-baseline difference from one paired change conflates the change with run-to-run variation.

Per-update effective_horizon and solver status were read for only 8 of 35 updates (0,5,10,15,20,25,30,34); the other 27 are unavailable, not absent, and no interpolation between sampled updates is asserted.

Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent); provider state, if a future run needs it, must come from the frozen provider bundle and any provider attempt is charged within the future grant.
arguments.hypothesis: A coordinate search over the two granted tip-speed weights (holding_tip_speed_weight starting at 0.05, terminal_tip_speed_weight starting at 0.0, both inside the granted domain [0.0,1.0]) is unlikely to restore joint reach/holding acceptance on this baseline: the retained evidence indicates the holding-speed failure is dominated by budget-limited plan selection rather than by the missing tip-speed penalty. A weight-only batch can only distinguish these accounts if some candidate with finite valid execution, force_bound_violation_n 0.0 and unchanged frozen acceptance reaches joint_reach_holding_passed true (holding_max_speed_m_s <= 0.02 m/s) while terminal_error_m stays within the 0.01 m tolerance.
arguments.rationale: The accepted revision and performed check leave the holding-speed failure better explained by budget-limited plan selection than by terminal-horizon truncation, and the one executed weight change (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0->0.05) is sealed as a physical_tradeoff with the sampled hold speed still ~59x the 0.02 m/s limit (F428 versus F456) while 35/35 updates miss their deadline (F75, F100) and mean complete-update time rose (F129). Even so, terminal_tip_speed_weight has never been varied (current 0.0), so a coordinate batch over both granted weights is the cheapest way to test whether any weight-only setting can move the joint reach/holding outcome before committing to a solve-budget intervention. The promise is therefore uncertain rather than promising: the evidence says weight-only tuning is a low-yield lever, but the terminal coordinate is untested and only 8 of 35 update records were inspected. The batch is planned with backend_solves = max_candidates, tool_calls >= 4*max_candidates, wall_s >= 990*max_candidates and 0 workers, consistent with the frozen protocol, and any provider attempt is bounded to the frozen bundle. No candidate is selected here, and recommendation dispositions (retained rec-defer-causal-replay and rec-defer-candidate-selection) are kept separate from this controller-candidate search plan.
stopping_conditions: Stop the batch after max_candidates = 6 candidate tell evaluations from search.family_coordinate@1.0.0.
Stop early only if a future authorized run yields joint_reach_holding_passed true with finite valid execution and force_bound_violation_n 0.0.
Stop if a coordinate step would leave the [0,1] domain of either weight or would generate a forbidden tiny positive value; each node uses 0 or a value >= 0.0001.
Treat any unevaluated or unreturned candidate as unavailable, never as evidence of improvement or of failure.
Do not promote or select any candidate in this stage; the plan is a future batch proposal and requires an explicit new grant.
If provider state is needed, attempt the frozen provider bundle once and record the attempt; do not escalate to backend replay or production changes within this stage.
weakening_observations: A candidate in the batch that reaches joint_reach_holding_passed true (holding_max_error_m <= 0.01 m and holding_max_speed_m_s <= 0.02 m/s) while terminal_error_m stays <= 0.01 m would weaken the budget-limited-selection account, since a weight-only change would then have closed the holding gap.

A monotone, large drop in holding_max_speed_m_s toward the 0.02 m/s limit as holding_tip_speed_weight or terminal_tip_speed_weight increases would weaken the claim that the tip-speed penalty is a minor contributor.

If the future bound comparison again classifies a candidate as physical_tradeoff or worse, or joint acceptance stays false in every candidate, the hypothesis that weight-only tuning is insufficient is strengthened rather than weakened.
